settings.title: App settings
settings.statsSectionHint: How often Open Planner Studio has been downloaded, per operating system and per release.
settings.statsIntro: How often Open Planner Studio has been downloaded. Public figures from GitHub Releases; nothing is collected from you.
settings.statsLinuxHint: * Linux counts installs and in-app updates together: the updater fetches the same .deb/.rpm/.AppImage that people also download by hand. Only the snap file counts as an installer.
settings.statsSource: GitHub Releases, updated weekly. As of {{date}}.
settings.statsError: The figures could not be fetched. Check your internet connection.
settings.statsSnapHint: Installs via the Snap Store do not go through GitHub and are not included here.
settings.languageHint: The app's display language, applied immediately.
settings.tourHint: Take the app's introductory tour again.
settings.showTaskTypesHint: Choose per task what adjusts when duration, units or work changes, like Task Type in MS Project and Duration Type in P6. Off: duration and units stay fixed. A file with task types or stored work shows them even when this is off.
settings.defaultTaskDurationUnitHint: Determines whether new tasks start in working days or working hours. Existing tasks do not change.
settings.durationDisplayHint: Controls how task duration is shown, independent of the unit a task itself is recorded in.
settings.durationDisplayOpsHint: In the OPS profile, each task shows its own unit.
settings.barSplitModeHint: For hour tasks only: split bars around breaks and non-working time. Actual task interruptions remain visible regardless of this setting.
settings.compressNonWorkdaysHint: Compresses the timeline: weekends and holidays from the project calendar are skipped, so a 5-workday task is exactly 5 columns wide.
settings.enableQuarterHourZoom: Show quarter-hours when zoomed in far
settings.enableQuarterHourZoomHint: Extra quarter-hour gradation on the hour time-scale when zoomed in far.
settings.weekStartDayHint: Week layout of the time scale.
settings.autoCalcCPMHint: Automatically recalculates the schedule as soon as it becomes out of date, instead of waiting for F5.
settings.constructionModeHint: On: construction-oriented defaults (a construction calendar with Dutch public holidays, builders' holiday, phasing templates). Off: a general, construction-neutral setup with a neutral default calendar. Only changes defaults for new projects; existing projects are unaffected.
settings.dragModeHint: Scroll wheel = zoom (anchored on the cursor) · Drag the chart background to pan the view. Dragging a task bar still moves that bar as usual. · Shift + scroll wheel scrolls through the rows · Ctrl/⌘ + drag draws a selection box.
settings.modifierMapHint: Choose which key performs each action. Picking a key that's already used swaps it with the other action.
settings.debugTerminalHint: Shows the log panel for troubleshooting.
settings.documentChromeHint: How you switch between open documents.
settings.dateNotationHint: Determines how dates are displayed everywhere in the app. Files and calculations are unaffected.
settings.timeNotationHint: Determines how clock times are displayed and entered: in the calendar window, for tasks in hours in the table, on the hour scale of the Gantt and in messages. Files and calculations are unaffected (24-hour).
settings.fontScaleHint: Scales the interface text and layout.
settings.fontHint: Web apps don't automatically follow your system font setting. Choose the font and size for the interface here.
settings.aiModeHint: Shows the AI tab with the MCP bridge, so AI assistants can work with your schedule over the Model Context Protocol. Turning it off stops the bridge.
settings.aiAutostartHint: Brings the MCP bridge live as soon as the app starts, so an AI client can connect without you opening the AI tab first. Desktop app only.
settings.classicViewControlsHint: Puts the separate Columns, Filter, Group and Sort buttons back on the View tab. You now choose columns with the plus in the table header or via Table → Columns…; filtering, grouping and sorting live in the layout buttons and the layout dialog.

welcome.title: Welcome to Open Planner Studio
welcome.introBody: Before you start: a few quick preferences, and an optional tour of the main areas.
welcome.tourStepBody: A short tour (7 steps) shows the main areas: tasks, planning, reports and more. You can stop at any time.

tour.step1Body: At the top you'll find the ribbon tabs. Each tab groups features around a theme, such as Start, Planning and Resources.
tour.step2Body: The task table is on the left, the Gantt chart on the right. This is where you plan and edit tasks and see the timeline.
tour.step3Body: Select a task to view and edit its details in this panel.
tour.step4Body: The histogram strip shows resource load below the Gantt chart — useful for spotting overallocation.
tour.step5Body: The Report tab lets you create printable overviews of your schedule.
tour.step6Body: Under File → Examples you'll find ready-made schedules to start from or learn from.
tour.step7Body: Missing something, found something clunky, or spotted a tiny bug — no matter how small? Let us know using this button. All feedback is welcome, truly every little thing helps make the app better.

preserveActualDatesInBackwardPass.label: Keep actual dates in the backward pass
preserveActualDatesInBackwardPass.help: With a status date, a completed task keeps its actual dates on the late side and a completed successor does not pull an open predecessor back into the past. An in-progress task keeps its actual start as late start, unless “In-progress task: early start = start of remaining work” is on. A completed task on a data-date point or window can still pass on relationship pressure.

clampNegativeFreeFloat.label: Free float never negative
clampNegativeFreeFloat.help: With an unachievable late constraint, total float stays negative but free float becomes zero.

p6ZeroDurationUsesPlannedBoundary.label: Milestone follows the planned calendar boundary
p6ZeroDurationUsesPlannedBoundary.help: Hour planning only. A zero-duration milestone follows the planned calendar boundary: a day start stays a start milestone, a working-block end may land on the predecessor’s finish. An ordinary zero-duration task can also get a boundary pair, but only with XER provenance as Task Dependent or Resource Dependent and a planned finish before its planned start.

p6UseTaskPlannedStartFloor.label: Planned start as an extra floor
p6UseTaskPlannedStartFloor.help: The planned start acts as a floor once both start and finish lie more than one calendar day later than the network allows. For a finish milestone with planned finish before planned start, a later planned start suffices. Excludes an in-progress task when “Planned start is not a floor for a task in progress” is on, and an unstarted ALAP task positioned from its successors. Does not require XER provenance.

p6FinishMilestoneBoundaryWindow.label: Finish milestone as a boundary window
p6FinishMilestoneBoundaryWindow.help: A zero-duration finish milestone gets a boundary window only if its planned finish is before its planned start and its calculated start still equals that planned start. A finish milestone with predecessors and no successor also gets its early dates as late dates, unless “Calculate float up to the project finish date” is on. Only seen in P3 output; off in every built-in profile.

p6PreserveActualInstants.label: Keep actual dates exact
p6PreserveActualInstants.help: Only for tasks with retained provenance from a .xer file. Recorded actual start and finish dates are not moved to the edge of a working block.

p6UseRemainingStartForProgress.label: In-progress task: early start = start of remaining work
p6UseRemainingStartForProgress.help: The early and late start of an in-progress task describe where the remaining work begins. Backward over a start-to-start relationship, only remaining duration counts, but only with hour planning, an actual start and progress between 0 and 100%, a known remaining duration smaller than the planned duration, and no elapsed duration or schedule splits. This extra remaining-duration rule does not apply to start-to-finish relationships.

p6PreserveZeroDurationConstraintInstants.label: Exact constraint moment on a milestone
p6PreserveZeroDurationConstraintInstants.help: Hour planning only, on the late side, for a date-and-time SNLT, MSO, FNLT or MFO constraint on a zero-duration milestone. The constraint moment stays exact, also at the start of a working block. In the forward pass, such a moment is already exact in every profile.

resumeFromActualElapsed.label: Remaining work resumes after the elapsed duration
resumeFromActualElapsed.help: An in-progress task resumes its remaining work no earlier than the actual start plus the elapsed duration. The status date and predecessor boundary remain lower limits; the latest of the three applies. Excludes Progress Override, tasks without remaining work, and cases where the app uses a valid resume date from the file (with at most one assignment).

unstartedIgnoresStatusDate.label: Don't move unstarted tasks to the status date
unstartedIgnoresStatusDate.help: Only with a status date, for a task without progress. That task is not moved to on or after the status date automatically.

p6RelationFinishBoundary.label: Successor starts on the finish boundary
p6RelationFinishBoundary.help: Only with hour planning on the predecessor’s calendar and for a relationship recognised by the app when opening a .xer file. For a finish-to-start relationship without lag where the file places the successor exactly at the predecessor’s working-block end, the successor starts at that finish. A relationship you add yourself is not covered. In the backward pass, the successor’s late start remains a working-block start.

p6BackwardLagFinishBoundary.label: Backward lag from a finish boundary
p6BackwardLagFinishBoundary.help: Only with hour planning on the calendar used for the lag. When the backward pass subtracts a positive working-time lag from an exact finish boundary and lands on the first working-block start of a day, it lands on the previous finish boundary. With a finish-to-finish relationship without lag, a late finish on a working-block end stays on that boundary. Excludes elapsed-time lag.

p6CompletedDataDateWindow.label: Completed task in the data-date window
p6CompletedDataDateWindow.help: Only with a status date, for completed leaf tasks from a .xer file with a retained target window, duration percent complete and P6 type Task Dependent or Resource Dependent with Fixed Duration & Units; excludes zero-duration milestones. Requires “In-progress task: early start = start of remaining work”. Suspend/resume is only allowed for Task Dependent with a valid pair, actual finish between planned finish and status date, resume no later than actual finish, and “Keep actual dates in the backward pass” on. The task gets early dates in the data-date window; its finish counts toward project finish.

p6CompletedLoeActualFinish.label: Completed LOE via its actual finish
p6CompletedLoeActualFinish.help: Only with a status date, for a completed LOE from a .xer file with positive duration, duration percent complete and P6 type Fixed Duration & Units/Time, a complete target window and actual finish between planned finish and status date. Requires at least one incoming relationship, all start-to-start, no successor and no suspend/resume. Requires “In-progress task: early start = start of remaining work”, “Keep actual dates in the backward pass” and “Keep actual dates exact”. The LOE follows its actual finish instead of the hammock route.

p6OpenLoeTargetSpan.label: Unstarted LOE uses the target window
p6OpenLoeTargetSpan.help: Hour planning only, for an unstarted LOE/hammock from a .xer file with 0% progress, positive duration, duration percent complete and P6 type Fixed Duration & Units; no actual dates or suspend/resume. Requires a complete positive target window whose start equals the relationship boundary and whose working time differs from the duration by at most one working day, at least one start-to-start input and one finish-to-finish output, only those relationship types and no lag. The LOE then uses the target window as its span. Weak evidence: one file.

p6CompletedPredecessorAtDataDate.label: Completed predecessor does not hold past the data date
p6CompletedPredecessorAtDataDate.help: Only with hour planning and a status date, for a completed predecessor with an actual finish. Finish-to-start and finish-to-finish relationships count from no later than the working boundary just before the status date; a later actual finish does not hold the successor back. Start-to-start and start-to-finish relationships stay on actual start. A completed task with its own data-date point or shifted data-date window follows that own boundary.

p6FreeFloatOnOwnCalendar.label: Free float in the task's own calendar
p6FreeFloatOnOwnCalendar.help: Hour planning only, for unfinished tasks and relationships with calculated free float. For an unstarted task, free float counts on its own calendar for finish-to-start, start-to-start and finish-to-finish, without elapsed-time or percentage lag. A non-zero lag requires the Predecessor lag calendar. For a started task, only finish-to-start without lag applies. The relationship’s own free float and driving flag do not change.

p6CompletedRemainingLag.label: Elapsed lag of a completed predecessor does not count
p6CompletedRemainingLag.help: Only with hour planning on the lag calendar and a status date, for completed predecessors from a .xer file with actual finish before the status date and a data-date point or window. Only the unelapsed part of a positive working-time lag counts. Applies on the late side and forward from a data-date point or shifted zero-remaining window. A task on its ordinary actual dates keeps the full lag; excludes elapsed-time lag.

p6CompletedOutOfSequenceWindow.label: Completed out-of-sequence task waits for its predecessors
p6CompletedOutOfSequenceWindow.help: Only with hour planning and a status date, on the XER route of “Completed task in the data-date window”; that convention and “In-progress task: early start = start of remaining work” must be on. Excludes Progress Override. Via finish-to-start or start-to-start inputs, the task gets the later of the data-date boundary and the boundary from an unfinished predecessor or one with a shifted data-date window. Ordinary completed predecessors do not count.

p6CompletedPhysicalAtDataDate.label: Completed physical-progress task sits at the data date
p6CompletedPhysicalAtDataDate.help: Only with hour planning and a status date, for completed leaf tasks and zero-duration milestones from a .xer file of P6 type Task Dependent, Start Milestone or Finish Milestone, with a retained target window, physical percent complete, actual finish no later than the status date and no suspend/resume. Requires “In-progress task: early start = start of remaining work”. The task sits at a single point on the data date, or later if a predecessor requires it. For other percent complete types, including duration, this is unmeasured and stays off.

p6InProgressStartLagElapsed.label: Elapsed SS lag from an in-progress predecessor does not count
p6InProgressStartLagElapsed.help: Only with hour planning on the lag calendar and a status date, for a start-to-start relationship with positive working-time lag from an unfinished predecessor with actual start before the status date. Requires “In-progress task: early start = start of remaining work”. Only the unelapsed part of the lag counts. “Calculate SS lag from an in-progress predecessor from” selects the anchor. Excludes elapsed-time lag.

p6FinishFinishStartMilestoneLateFinish.label: Finish-to-finish relationship to a start milestone binds to the milestone itself
p6FinishFinishStartMilestoneLateFinish.help: Only with hour planning on both sides of a finish-to-finish relationship to a zero-duration start milestone. The relationship binds to the milestone itself: the predecessor’s late finish may run up to the milestone’s late finish. Free float may also change; the milestone’s early start stays unchanged. Excludes finish milestones and the backward zero-remaining-duration route.

p6StartedTaskIgnoresPlannedStartFloor.label: Planned start is not a floor for a task in progress
p6StartedTaskIgnoresPlannedStartFloor.help: Only for a task with actual start and less than 100% progress, when “Planned start as an extra floor” is on. Its planned start adds no floor for remaining work; the status date and its predecessors still apply.

p6LateFinishOnOwnCalendar.label: Late finish on the task's own calendar
p6LateFinishOnOwnCalendar.help: Only with hour planning, when a successor boundary determines late finish and no tighter constraint or deadline replaces that boundary. If it falls outside the task’s own working time, late finish becomes the end of the previous work period on its own calendar. Excludes a late finish determined by project finish.

p6ProgressOverrideIgnoresStartedSuccesso.label: Progress Override ignores a started successor on the late side too
p6ProgressOverrideIgnoresStartedSuccesso.help: Only under Progress Override, for an unfinished predecessor and a started but unfinished successor (actual start or progress). Their relationship does not count in the predecessor’s late dates and free float.

p6FinishNotBeforeFinishFinishBound.label: Early finish not before a finish-to-finish boundary
p6FinishNotBeforeFinishFinishBound.help: Date correction: for a finish-to-finish relationship with working-time lag, without hammocks and with hour planning on both the successor’s calendar (for remaining work: its progress calendar) and the lag calendar. If the relationship boundary is later than early finish with no working time between them, only finish moves to the first working boundary on or after it. Applies to automatically scheduled unstarted and in-progress successors; an unstarted task’s hard finish pin takes precedence. Free float: separately, for a zero-lag finish-to-finish relationship without percentage lag, an unfinished predecessor with existing relationship free float and a calculated successor early finish counts from its own early finish to the successor’s early finish on its own hour calendar. This also applies to zero elapsed-time lag, with no extra hour-planning condition on the successor or lag calendar. Hammocks and manually scheduled tasks ultimately keep free float at zero.

p6AlapPositionedFromSuccessors.label: ALAP tasks as late as the successors allow
p6AlapPositionedFromSuccessors.help: Hour planning only, for an unstarted task that is not manually scheduled and has the “As late as possible” (ALAP) constraint. Its successors’ early dates determine its position to the minute; successors go first. Its own planned start does not count; predecessors, status date and a second constraint still apply. Without a successor, it uses its late finish. The ordinary ALAP step remains available in every profile.

milestoneWithoutPredecessorAtDayEnd.label: Isolated milestones at the end of the workday
milestoneWithoutPredecessorAtDayEnd.help: An isolated milestone or a finish milestone without a predecessor is placed at the end of its workday.

tutorialOffer.title: Tutorials
tutorialOffer.question: Would you like to make your first schedule with a tutorial now?
tutorialOffer.body: The tour is done. In tutorial 1 you build a schedule for a house extension step by step; a panel gives you one instruction at a time and notices when you have done it. The tutorials are an extension: if it is not installed yet, the app downloads it and first asks whether you trust it.

xer.name: Primavera file (.xer)
xer.kept: The app took over the WBS and the activities, with relationships, calendars, resources, progress, activity codes and user-defined fields. A baseline project becomes the baseline of the project that refers to it.
xer.limited: A relationship between two projects does not become a relationship in your schedule. If the calculation differs, you first see the dates as Primavera saved them.
xer.save: Save writes a new IFC file, with the original .xer inside it. Writing back to .xer is not possible: your .xer never changes.

mpp.name: MS Project file (.mpp)
mpp.kept: The app took over tasks with their structure, duration and constraints, plus relationships, calendars, resources, assignments and progress.
mpp.limited: Baselines, costs and rates, notes and MS Project's custom fields are not included. If the calculation differs, you first see the dates as MS Project saved them.
mpp.save: Save writes a new IFC file: your .mpp never changes. Writing back to .mpp is not possible. Exporting to MS Project XML is.

mspdi.name: MS Project XML
mspdi.kept: The app took over tasks with their structure, plus relationships, constraints, calendars, resources, assignments, progress, the status date and baseline 0.
mspdi.limited: Notes, activity codes and custom fields are not included. The project calculates with the Open Planner Studio profile, not as Microsoft Project.
mspdi.save: Save writes a new IFC file: your XML file does not change. You can write back with Export › MS Project XML.

p6xml.name: Primavera P6 XML
p6xml.kept: The app took over the WBS and the tasks, with relationships, constraints, calendars, resources, assignments, progress and the status date. A baseline project becomes a baseline of the project it belongs to.
p6xml.limited: Deadlines, activity codes, custom fields and notes are not included. The project calculates with the Open Planner Studio profile, not as Primavera P6.
p6xml.save: Save writes a new IFC file: your XML file does not change. You can write back with Export › Primavera P6 XML.

csv.name: CSV file
csv.kept: The app read one task per row: name, WBS code, duration, dates, predecessors and progress.
csv.limited: A CSV contains no resources, calendars, constraints, deadlines or baselines. The project is called CSV Import.
csv.save: Save writes a new IFC file: your CSV does not change. You can write back with Export › CSV (semicolon-separated).

ifcSchemaQuestion.title: Which IFC schema to save in?
ifcSchemaQuestion.body: This file was saved as {{schema}}. The app saves as IFC 4.3 ADD2 by default, the schema of IfcOpenShell and Bonsai. Do you want to keep this file as {{schema}}? You can change this later in Project settings.
ifcSchemaQuestion.bodyUnwritable: This file was saved as {{schema}}. The app cannot write that schema. Choose the schema in which the app saves it. You can change this later in Project settings.
